I'm running a parallel process model with 3 groups: 1)everyone N used=1056, 2)Younger group N used=263; 3)older group N used =250.

Group 1 and 3: ran fine but with warnings that says
> fit11 <- growth(model11, data = Participants)
Warning message:
In lav_object_post_check(object) :

I researched this online and I believe it means that my model is mis-specified and/or my model fit is poor.


2)younger group gives me a warning that optimizer warns that a solution has not been found, and an error that model did not converge. details below.

Based on my research online, I think it means that model fit is poor If the model does not converge,
If I'm testing a hypothesis with this model, is there anything that I can do or do I just report that the model fit was poor?

messages.author: edceb8dce9472a62
messages.subject: Re: LGCM- model did not converge error
parts:
Your data does not reflect the model you imposed, yes. 

You can try to assess the construct over time in ggplot (or base R) to see if the data looks to be linearly increasing over time. You don't have enough data points to try higher orders of fit, but it's possible one/both of these only has a significant intercept term (i.e., doesn't increase over time). If that is the case, you could have an intercept-only (for one construct) and intercept and slope, instead of the PPM you presented.

Get fit for just 1 latent growth curve first, and if it fits well, put it with the other latent growth curve. (These estimates are not trustable, but best guess suggests s2 with a near 0 intercept and variance might be causing the trouble.)

I don't think this will help with convergence, but you might want to look into grouping your large data file (dat) into just the young and old groups and making a grouping variable, then following the instructions here (https://lavaan.ugent.be/tutorial/groups.html). 

For example: 

library(tidyverse)
small_dat<-dat %>% filter(age < ## | age > ##) 

small_dat$Group <- ifelse(small_dat$age < ##, "Young", "Old")

Then call the Lavaan object 

fit <- growth(model, data = small_dat, group = "Group")

and when you call summary(fit), you'll get both group's results.

Hope this helps, 
Chris
